meta_title: Kai Shin Digital Infrastructure Inc. | Operator of a GW-class Data Center Project in Southern Kyushu
meta_desc: Kai Shin Digital Infrastructure Inc. (凱信数基株式会社) develops and operates an AI data center in Satsumasendai, Kagoshima, starting at 350MW and targeting 1GW. A joint venture of CDIB Capital and Shinetsu Science Industry, building a GW-class AI computing foundation in southern Kyushu powered by decarbonized electricity.
nav_013: Kai Shin Digital Infrastructure Inc. — Satsumasendai, Kagoshima 1GW AI Data Center Cluster
nav_014:
Opening computing power that accelerates existing industries to the region
Developing, producing and selling industry — and accelerating its maintenance
nav_015: In Satsumasendai, Kagoshima, we are developing an AI data center cluster of up to 1GW on a site of approximately 37 hectares. Aiming to create businesses that accelerate the design, procurement, construction, logistics and maintenance of existing industries, we are building an active economic engine that generates continuous investment and employment.
nav_017: GW-class clean power, the passion of Kagoshima's people, and a new growth engine for southern Kyushu following TSMC Kumamoto
nav_019: Kyushu Electric Power mix — 65% green & clean energy
nav_021: Serious, fast-moving local government support and a passionate prefectural spirit
nav_022: A growth pillar following TSMC Kumamoto
nav_023: An industrial base for semiconductors and next-generation industries
nav_024: Kagoshima is one of the rare regions able to supply GW-class clean power stably over the long term, and through the united efforts of its passionate residents and government it has the foundation to host advanced industries. Adjacent to Sendai Port, a designated major port, it holds advantages in both logistics and communications. Linked to the expansion of the semiconductor supply chain radiating from TSMC Kumamoto, it will become a new growth engine for southern Kyushu — a hub supplying computing power to all of Japan with AI data centers at its core.
nav_026: Ripple effects on the regional economy that cloud data centers cannot offer, AI-driven advancement of manufacturing, and an AIDC operator born of Japan–Taiwan collaboration
nav_028: Direct economic impact from large-scale power demand and capital investment
nav_030: A revolution in design, manufacturing, logistics, development and sales through AI
nav_032: The birth of an AIDC operator formed by Japan and Taiwan
nav_033: Unlike conventional cloud facilities, AI data centers require high-density power and advanced equipment, generating large-scale capital investment and power demand in the region. They also attract the talent needed for sophisticated operations, raising the quality of employment. Furthermore, through collaboration with the semiconductor and AI industries they induce the clustering of related companies, becoming the core infrastructure that transforms the regional economy from a consumption-based to a production- and creation-based one.
nav_034: Alignment with the national GX strategy
nav_035: In step with national strategy and local government, creating local AI demand and revitalizing the design, manufacturing, logistics and sales of Japanese industry through AI
nav_037: A fiber-optic network from Kagoshima connecting to Asia and Oceania
nav_038: Containerized logistics at the Port of Satsumasendai
nav_039: An adjacent port introducing container logistics — the development and revolution of logistics
nav_041: Local job creation arising from infrastructure construction and maintenance
nav_042: This plan aligns with the Japanese government's GX policy and its policy of regionally distributed data centers, building GX-type infrastructure premised on renewable and low-carbon power. With advanced semiconductors and the AI data centers that utilize them at its core, it creates local AI demand within Japan while fostering and creating operators rooted in the region. Japanese businesses take an active role in facilities and operations, and through industry–government–academia collaboration the project generates a sustainable industrial base and new business opportunities for the region.
nav_044: Full-scale operation of a large AI data center
nav_045: Expanding in stages from 350MW to bring a large-scale AI data center into full operation. Extra-high-voltage substations, battery storage and liquid/air cooling are deployed in earnest to handle large AI training and inference workloads. With a co-located Wistron AI server assembly plant and the port logistics of Sendai Port at its core, we build a regional supply chain that integrates everything from component procurement to installation.
nav_047: Expanding to a cluster of up to 1GW to establish a domestic AI foundation spanning LLM creation through the social implementation of Physical AI. Contributing to the competitiveness of precision manufacturing with RAG-based LLMs for IC design, while fostering domestic players across every field of AI data centers and forming an industrial ecosystem rooted in the region.
